title: Gaining knowledge
intro: The very first word revealed in the Qur’an was “Read!” – seeking knowledge is a Muslim’s lifelong duty.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Read in the name of your Lord who created – created the human being from a clinging clot. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught the human being what he did not know. <small>(Qur’an, Al-‘Alaq 96:1–5)</small>

The first words of the Qur’an revealed to Muhammad (SAW) were about reading, learning and gaining knowledge. These are qualities only a human being can practise, and through them people are raised above all other creatures. A person can believe without knowledge, but such belief often goes astray. Only with true knowledge can a person understand the real meaning of faith and of this short life in the dunya.

Following that first revelation, Muslims must make their souls noble with knowledge and good behaviour. Knowledge is a strong motivation for how we behave and act, but it also brings responsibility. The knowledge we gain should be put into practice: we act by it, and through it we guide others to good and keep them from evil. A Muslim must also pass on the knowledge they have gained to other people.

In the very first revelation Allah commanded Iqra’ – read, learn, study and keep growing in knowledge until the end of life. Sadly, many Muslims today have neglected this Qur’anic command, and they lag behind in education around the world.

learn.title: Use your youth
learn.html: It is especially important to use our youth for learning. A wise saying says that learning when young is like carving in stone – it stays with us our whole life and helps us in every situation.
In other places in the Qur’an, too, Allah (SWT) stresses knowledge and the value of people of learning. He draws our attention to their worth:

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: He gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever has been given wisdom has been given a great good. But only people of understanding remember this. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Baqarah 2:269)</small>
Allah (SWT) teaches us a dua and commands us to learn so that we increase our knowledge:

learn.label: Dua for knowledge (Qur’an, Ta-Ha 20:114)
learn.en: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: Muhammad (SAW) described seeking knowledge as a path to Jannah. He said: “Whoever follows a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Jannah.” (Muslim)

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: We must gain knowledge all our life – knowledge that benefits the one who has it, and through them all people. It takes giving things up, work, effort, patience and sacrifice.

“He gives wisdom to whom He wills”
A path to Jannah for the one who seeks knowledge

practice.title: Knowledge brings responsibility
practice.prompt: Tap what a Muslim should do with the knowledge they gain, then tap Check.

options.text: 🧭 Use it to guide others to good
🗣️ Pass it on to other people

options.why: A Muslim must pass on the knowledge they have gained to others.
We seek knowledge our whole life – until the end.
Knowledge should make the soul noble and lead to good behaviour, not pride.

questions.q: What was the first command Allah gave in the Qur’an?
What raises a human being above other creatures?
What is learning in youth like, according to the wise saying?
Which dua did Allah teach us for knowledge?
What does Allah make easy for the one who seeks knowledge?
How long should we keep learning?

practice.title: Questions and talk
prompts: 📖 What was the first command Allah (SWT) gave to people?
💡 What is the role of knowledge in a Muslim’s life? What is the best time of life for learning?
♾️ What is lifelong learning? Do you know someone around you who keeps learning all their life?
🎓 Talk with your muallim: plan your path through education. After middle school, think about high school and college. Which subjects interest you, and what work would you like to do?
